clue.text: You would have to lie about this measure for linden

indicators.note: the clue tells the solver that something must be wrapped round the answer to reach the tree, so the answer is that tree minus the wrapping
the word lie has to go round this answer, so taking those outer letters away leaves it

parts.note: the linden is another name for the lime tree
taken as written

explanation.surface: An odd instruction to tell a fib about a certain unit when describing a tree.
explanation.walkthrough: 'You would have to' and 'about this' turn the clue inside out: wrapping the word lie round the answer would make the linden's other name, so strip those letters from that name.
explanation.definitionFit: A metre is a unit of length, so it is a measure; it is also a verse rhythm.

clue.text: So far it's revealing, by the way

definitions.text: So far it's revealing, by the way

parts.words: So far it's revealing, by the way
parts.note: a roadside stone that shows how many miles remain or have been travelled, set beside the way

explanation.definitionFit: A roadside marker stone shows distances along the road, revealing how far one has come.

clue.text: Draw line at sea creature of supernatural kind

definitions.meaning: to fish by trailing a line behind a moving boat
a giant or dwarf of Scandinavian folklore

explanation.surface: A fisherman draws in his line and finds a sea monster.
explanation.definitionFit: To trail a fishing line from a boat is to troll; Norse folklore's ugly giants also bear the name.

clue.text: Give right name

definitions.meaning: to grant someone a claim or permission
to give a book or film a title

explanation.definitionFit: To entitle is both to grant someone a claim and to give a work its title.

clue.text: Small bowls put on part of table for biscuits

indicators.note: in an across answer one piece placed on another follows it, so the bowls come after the table part

parts.note: a flap is the hinged leaf of a drop-leaf table
in the game of bowls the jack is the small target ball, so jacks are small bowls

explanation.surface: Someone arranges little dishes on the table to hold biscuits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Small bowls' suggests dishes; in lawn bowls the jack is the small white ball players aim at.
explanation.definitionFit: In Britain flapjacks are chewy oat-and-syrup bars, eaten like biscuits.

clue.text: Enemy intended, we hear, to cause agitation

indicators.note: we hear points to the sound of the words, not their spelling

parts.note: a foe is an enemy and meant means intended

explanation.surface: An opponent meant, by repute, to stir up trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: FOE MEANT (Enemy intended) said aloud gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To foment is to stir up trouble or unrest.

clue.text: Lyrics? Many are transported by them

definitions.meaning: the words to a tune, read as lines of an air

explanation.surface: Song words carry many people away emotionally.
explanation.walkthrough: 'transported' suggests being carried away by a song; read literally it means flown.
explanation.definitionFit: Words of a song are lines of an air; carriers that fly passengers are the other sense.

clue.text: Preserve this island, in short

parts.note: a word for a fruit preserve is also the three-letter short code for this Caribbean island

explanation.walkthrough: JAM, a preserve, is the island's standard three-letter abbreviation, as used in international country codes.
explanation.definitionFit: The Caribbean island nation is shortened to JAM in official country codes.

clue.text: Special business group to pledge support for driver

parts.note: to commit is to pledge
in golf the ball is placed on a tee before being hit with a driver

explanation.surface: A dedicated firm promises to back the man at the wheel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'driver' suggests a motorist; it is the golf club, and the tee supports the ball for it.
explanation.definitionFit: A committee is a small group appointed to handle particular business.

clue.text: Military HQ, initially, such as Pentagon

definitions.meaning: the initials of NATO's Supreme Headquarters Allied Powers Europe
a pentagon is a geometric figure

explanation.surface: Military headquarters, at first, like the Pentagon building.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pentagon' looks like the US defence building; it is the five-sided figure.
explanation.definitionFit: NATO's European command is known by its initials; a pentagon is a geometric form.

clue.text: Mistake in ring terminal for him?

indicators.note: a mistake garbles things, so the letters that follow are put into a new order

parts.note: a ring is round like the letter O

explanation.surface: A single slip in the circus ring could be fatal for the man in charge of the big cats.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mistake' rearranges O (ring) with TERMINAL. The whole clue also describes the answer: a slip in the ring can be fatal for him.
explanation.definitionFit: The 'him' of the clue is the circus performer who works with big cats in the ring.

clue.text: Dance, nonetheless, with a snake

indicators.note: read as none-less: the letter O, meaning nothing or none, is taken away

parts.note: the mambo is a Latin American dance

explanation.surface: Someone dances regardless, accompanied by a serpent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nonetheless' looks like 'even so'; read as 'none less' it drops O (nothing) from MAMBO, giving MAMB.
explanation.definitionFit: The mamba is a fast, highly venomous African snake.

clue.text: Divided four in endless affront to purist

parts.note: something divided has been split

indicators.note: the Roman numeral for four goes inside the word for endless

parts.note: endless means infinite
IV is four in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: Something split four ways in a never-ending insult to a stickler.
explanation.definitionFit: Grammatical purists object to putting a word between 'to' and its verb, as in 'to boldly go'.

clue.text: Bird circles the fish it hunts

parts.note: circles are rings, each shaped like the letter O, so O's
what a hunter chases is its prey

explanation.surface: A bird wheels round over the fish it is hunting.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is true of the bird itself, which feeds on fish it hunts from the air.
explanation.definitionFit: The osprey is a large fish-eating hawk.

clue.text: Artificial solution to problems of beat generation

definitions.text: Artificial solution to problems of beat generation

parts.words: Artificial solution to problems of beat generation
parts.note: a device implanted to keep an irregular heart beating steadily

explanation.walkthrough: 'beat generation' suggests the 1950s writers; it means the producing of a heartbeat.
explanation.definitionFit: An implanted electronic device regulates a faulty heart rhythm.

clue.text: Particularly nice as a master

definitions.meaning: nice in its old sense of fussy and precise, particularly so: overly exact about details
like a pedant, a word that once meant a schoolmaster

explanation.surface: Someone being especially pleasant in the role of a teacher.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nice' here is the old sense, finely exact, not pleasant; 'pedant' originally meant a schoolmaster.
explanation.definitionFit: Being fussily exact about small details is the mark of a pedant, a word once used for a schoolteacher.

clue.text: City or third-grade village

parts.note: grades run A, B, C, so the third grade is C
Ambridge is the fictional village in the long-running BBC radio soap The Archers

explanation.surface: Is it a city or just a poor sort of village?
explanation.walkthrough: AMBRIDGE is the village setting of The Archers, a long-running BBC radio soap opera.
explanation.definitionFit: Cambridge is an English university city.

clue.text: Sort of, house never used as academy

parts.note: a semi, short for semi-detached, is a sort of British house sharing one wall with its neighbour
nary is used, chiefly in dialect, for never or not one, as in nary a word

explanation.surface: A kind of house that has never been used as a school.
explanation.walkthrough: A semi is a semi-detached house, a common British type; 'nary' is dialect for not one.
explanation.definitionFit: A seminary is a college or school, especially one training priests.

clue.text: Incorporated one conclusion in another

indicators.note: one word for a conclusion is placed inside a second word for the same idea

parts.note: another conclusion, an end
a close is a conclusion

explanation.surface: A deduction folded inside a further deduction.
explanation.walkthrough: 'conclusion' suggests a deduction from reasoning; here both conclusions are simply endings, one set 'in' the other.
explanation.definitionFit: Something incorporated is contained or included within something else.

clue.text: Speakers taking on raw Tory so inconclusively

indicators.note: each word is left without its conclusion, so the final letter of every word goes

explanation.surface: Public speakers taking on a crude Conservative and trailing off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'inconclusively' cuts the last letter from each of 'on raw Tory so', leaving O, RA, TOR and S.
explanation.definitionFit: Orators are people who make speeches in public.

clue.text: Second best source of amusement

parts.note: the cream is the best part, as in the cream of the crop

explanation.surface: The runner-up turns out to be the most entertaining thing.
explanation.definitionFit: A very funny person or thing is called a scream, as in 'she's a scream'.

clue.text: Norman's residence, perhaps, where his pet gets water

parts.note: a Norman, being French, would call his pet cat a chat
eau is French for water

explanation.surface: A Norman's house is where his cat gets its drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Norman' signals French: the Normandy native's cat is a CHAT and his water EAU.
explanation.definitionFit: A French country house or castle, the kind of home a man from Normandy might own.

clue.text: Ruined like John and Anne

definitions.meaning: the poet John Donne and his wife Anne, punned on as one Donne and another

explanation.surface: A couple named John and Anne brought to ruin.
explanation.walkthrough: After his secret marriage cost him his post, the poet John Donne wrote 'John Donne, Anne Donne, Un-done'.
explanation.definitionFit: Being undone means being ruined; the poet Donne punned on his own surname this way.

clue.text: Steps on board to run after mate

indicators.note: the word for a run comes after the word for a mate

parts.note: a mate is a companion
a run in tights or stockings is a ladder in British usage

explanation.surface: Climbing aboard in order to chase a friend.
explanation.walkthrough: 'run' is a ladder, the British word for a run in tights; 'on board' means aboard ship, where steps between decks have this name.
explanation.definitionFit: On ships, the steep stairway from deck to cabin has this name.

clue.text: TUC split

parts.note: in a down answer the word for split, read as an instruction, puts the word cut upwards, giving these three letters

explanation.walkthrough: TUC is the British Trades Union Congress; the answer read as an instruction (CUT, UP in a down light) turns CUT into TUC.
explanation.definitionFit: To cut something up is to split it into pieces.

clue.text: Bananas or nuts are, say, in-eluded in plan

indicators.note: the sound of the word are goes into the word for crazy

parts.note: bananas and nuts are both slang for daft, crazy

indicators.note: say means the word is to be heard, not read

parts.note: said aloud, these words sound like R

explanation.surface: Fruit or nuts, say, form part of a scheme.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bananas or nuts' look like food; both mean crazy, DAFT. 'are, say' is the letter R by sound.
explanation.definitionFit: A draft is a preliminary version or plan.

clue.text: Capital, moreover, holding key out East?

indicators.note: the word for moreover keeps the trimmed key inside it

parts.note: too means moreover, also

indicators.note: the letter for East is put out of the word key

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A capital city that also keeps a key, out in the Orient?
explanation.walkthrough: 'out East' looks like a hint at the Far East, where the city is; instead 'out' removes the East abbreviation from key before 'holding' puts what is left inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Japan's seat of government is Tokyo, its capital city.

clue.text: Mentioned earlier, as idea for reform

indicators.note: to reform is to form again, so the letters are reshaped

explanation.surface: A suggestion made beforehand for political reform.
explanation.definitionFit: A legal word for what was referred to above or before in a text.

clue.text: Columns lined up for Priestley novel

indicators.note: novel means new, so the name is made new by rearranging

explanation.surface: Lined-up columns for a book by J. B. Priestley.
explanation.walkthrough: 'novel' looks like a book by the writer J. B. Priestley; it is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A peristyle is a row of columns surrounding a courtyard or building.

clue.text: Release capital from BBC

indicators.note: the capital, or first, letter is taken from the BBC's nickname

parts.note: Auntie, or Auntie Beeb, is the British nickname for the BBC

explanation.surface: Free the capital city from the British broadcaster.
explanation.walkthrough: 'capital' suggests London; it means a first letter. The BBC is nicknamed Auntie in Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: To untie something is to set it free by undoing knots.
